title: Bluetooth: Add 5.3 control procs, and mark incorrect control proc collision resolution
description:
**Part 1**: Detect invalid control procedure collision resolution

**Part 2**: Add and fix existing 5.2 and 5.3 control procedure dissection 


In Bluetooth core specification v5.3, Vol 6, Part B, Section 5.3, it is described how control procedure collisions should be handled when both devices initiate incompatible procedures. This PR adds adds expert information if the collision is not resolved according to the specification. This makes it easier to read logs and diagnose issues.

Example of an invalid scenario:
```
M->S: LL_PHY_REQ
S->M: LL_PHY_REQ
S->M: LL_PHY_RSP
M->S: LL_PHY_UPDATE_IND  # The master is not allowed to continue the procedure here
```
The correct sequence for this scenario is:
```
M->S: LL_PHY_REQ
S->M: LL_PHY_REQ
S->M: LL_PHY_RSP
M->S: LL_REJECT_EXT_IND
M->S: LL_PHY_UPDATE_IND
```

To be able to perform the analysis required, I've first refactored some of the code that starts, adds control procedure frames, and completes control procedures. This removes duplicate code, makes it less error-prone, and makes it easier to utilize this for future control procedures. See each individual commit for more details.

Some control procedure validation for control procedures added in 5.1 - 5.3 were partly added in https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/2283. That commit contained some missing control procedure handling and missing procedures. Those have been added here.  

To validate the implementation I've performed manual inspection of manually generated logs.
1. [single_control_procs.pcap](/uploads/012c1e80049d9d43d7d06f03cfa868d1/single_control_procs.pcap). Contains the set of all valid control procedure sequences. No expert info is added to this file as it only contains valid sequences.
2. [concurrent_control_procs.pcap](/uploads/d99ae61cf309330e48e1d0be36940655/concurrent_control_procs.pcap). Contains a large set of valid concurrent control procedures sequences. The first part contains sequences where none of the initiated procedures contain instants. The second part contains collision scenarios where the master correctly rejects the slave initiated procedure. No expert info is added to this file as it only contains valid sequences.
3. [concurrent_control_procs_invalid_resolution.pcap](/uploads/b1500a54d5f458c204e7a62c149ca5c8/concurrent_control_procs_invalid_resolution.pcap). Contains a set of control procedures sequences where the master is not correctly aborting the incompatible peripheral initiated procedure. For each sequence expert information is added.

Let me know if you would rather have this PR split up.

commits_data.title: Bluetooth: Detect invalid incompatible control procedure conflict resolution
commits_data.message:
Bluetooth: Detect invalid incompatible control procedure conflict resolution

Core spec 5.2, Vol 6, Part B, Section 5.3 describes how the link layer should
resolve the scenario where a collision occurs where both link layers initiate
incompabile control procedures.

This commit adds expect information for the case where these conflicts are not
handled according to spec.

Example of an invalid scenario:

M->S: LL_PHY_REQ
S->M: LL_PHY_REQ
S->M: LL_PHY_RSP
M->S: LL_PHY_UPDATE_IND

The correct sequence for this scenario is:
M->S: LL_PHY_REQ
S->M: LL_PHY_REQ
S->M: LL_PHY_RSP
M->S: LL_REJECT_EXT_IND
M->S: LL_PHY_UPDATE_IND

Signed-off-by: Rubin Gerritsen <rubin.gerritsen@nordicsemi.no>

commits_data.title: Bluetooth: Refactor adding control procedure packets to contexts
commits_data.message:
Bluetooth: Refactor adding control procedure packets to contexts

By defining control_proc_add_frame(), control_proc_add_last_frame(), and
control_proc_add_frame_with_instant() a lot of duplicate code can be removed.

This commit makes the checks for the CIS establishment procedure follow the spec.
Previously the dissector had two bugs:
 - It allowed both master and slave to initiate this procedure
 - The procedure was marked as complete once the LL_CIS_RSP was received.

Signed-off-by: Rubin Gerritsen <rubin.gerritsen@nordicsemi.no>

commits_data.title: Bluetooth: Refactor starting control proc context
commits_data.message:
Bluetooth: Refactor starting control proc context

Moves the check of starting a control procedure before the previous was complete inside
the function control_proc_start(). This check should be beformed before starting any
control procedure. Therefore it is better to simply move it inside the funciton to remove
code duplication.

Signed-off-by: Rubin Gerritsen <rubin.gerritsen@nordicsemi.no>
